name: BitoPro
rootCause: According to on-chain investigator ZachXBT, crypto exchange BitoPro was reportedly hacked on May 8, 2025, resulting in losses of approximately $11.5 million. The attacker drained assets from BitoPro’s hot wallets on Tron, Ethereum, Solana, and Polygon, then sold them via DEXs. The stolen funds were subsequently laundered through Tornado Cash or bridged via Thorchain to the Bitcoin network, eventually ending up in a Wasabi Wallet. BitoPro stated that the tactics used in this incident closely resemble those seen in several major international cases, attributing the attack to the North Korean hacking group Lazarus.

The attacker drained assets from BitoPro’s hot wallets on Tron, Ethereum, Solana, and Polygon, then sold them via DEXs. The stolen funds were subsequently laundered through Tornado Cash or bridged via Thorchain to the Bitcoin network, eventually ending up in a Wasabi Wallet. BitoPro stated that the tactics used in this incident closely resemble those seen in several major international cases, attributing the attack to the North Korean hacking group Lazarus.

On May 8, 2025, BitoPro's hot wallets on Ethereum, Tron, Solana, and Polygon were compromised during a wallet infrastructure upgrade, resulting in a theft of approximately $11.5 million. The breach stemmed from hijacked AWS session tokens, which allowed attackers to bypass multi-factor authentication and conduct unauthorized withdrawals. Attackers gained access to the exchange's cloud infrastructure by hijacking an employee's AWS session tokens via social engineering and malware, enabling them to bypass MFA and inject malicious scripts during a wallet upgrade.
